title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a working sheet from the 'Teichmülleries' (1981–83). It computes generators and relations for a surface mapping class group, extended by orientation-reversing symmetries.

(1) Drawings. The top-left sketch shows a surface: a ring-like handle crossed by a tube. It is labelled with pieces X', X_0^* and with curves ε' (or ε̄'), e'' and an arrow-marked loop. The second sketch is the same kind of surface seen differently. The third shows a cellular decomposition, with the counts 'four rectangles, 10 edges, 4 vertices'. That gives χ = 4 − 10 + 4 = −2, so the surface has type (g,n) with 2g − 2 + n = 2. Candidates are a closed genus-2 surface, a two-holed torus, or a four-holed sphere; the pictures suggest a handle configuration. The small circle with a hatched sector is probably a local picture at a vertex or puncture.

(2) Symmetries. τ, τ', τ'' are involutions that pairwise commute: τ'^2 = τ''^2 = τ^2 = (τ''τ)^2 = (τ τ')^2 = (τ'τ'')^2 = 1. An attempted longer relation is crossed out. So they generate a Klein-type group (Z/2)^2 or (Z/2)^3.

(3) Action on the twists. ε_0, ε_1, ε_2 are Dehn twists along a chain of three curves.
- τ swaps ε_0 and ε_2 and inverts ε_1: τ(ε_0) = ε_2, τ(ε_1) = ε_1^{-1}.
- τ' and τ'' invert every ε_i.
- An involution sends a twist to its inverse exactly when it reverses orientation and preserves the curve. So τ, τ', τ'' are reflections, i.e. anti-holomorphic involutions or 'real structures'.
- τ'τ'' fixes every ε_i; it is plausibly the hyperelliptic involution, or the identity on this subgroup.
The images of the generators are then checked:
- [ε_0, ε_2] = 1, since disjoint curves give commuting twists.
- ρ_0 := (ε_1ε_0)^{-1} = ε_0^{-1}ε_1^{-1}.
- τ(ρ_0) = (ε_1^{-1}ε_2)^{-1} = ε_2^{-1}ε_1 =: ρ_2. This is correct, since τ is a homomorphism.

(4) Relations of the torus piece. The circled relation is (ε_1ε_0)^6 = 1 = (ε_0ε_1ε_0)^4. From the braid relation ε_0ε_1ε_0 = ε_1ε_0ε_1, written as ε_0(ε_1ε_0) = (ε_1ε_0)ε_1, he derives (ε_1ε_0)^3 = (ε_0ε_1ε_0)^2. In SL_2(Z) terms, with σ_0 = ε_0ε_1ε_0 (playing the role of S) and ρ_0^{-1} = ε_1ε_0, this is ρ_0^{-3} = σ_0^2 = −I. That is exactly the presentation of Γ_{1,1} for a once-punctured torus, i.e. of SL_2(Z).

(5) Transport by τ. An arrow carries the relation through τ, giving ε_2ε_1^{-1}ε_2 = ε_1^{-1}ε_2ε_1^{-1}. This is τ applied to the braid relation ε_0ε_1ε_0 = ε_1ε_0ε_1, and it is correct; it is equivalent to the braid relation between ε_1 and ε_2.

Purpose. Within Grothendieck's Lego–Teichmüller programme, the sheet assembles a presentation of a genus-2 / type-(1,2) modular group and its extension by reflections. It does so from the basic pieces Γ_{1,1} (≅ SL_2(Z)) and the braid relations, using the symmetry τ to transport relations from one handle to the other.
errors: The relation (ε_1ε_0)^6 = 1 holds in the mapping class group of a once-punctured torus. In a closed genus-2 surface, or a torus with two holes or punctures, the chain relation gives (ε_1ε_0)^6 = twist along the boundary of the torus neighbourhood of ε_0 ∪ ε_1, which is nontrivial there. So the circled relation is valid only locally, inside a Γ_{1,1}-piece, or modulo that separating twist. The sheet does not make this explicit.
The parenthetical '(τ(ε_2) = τ(ε_1))' in the transcription cannot be right as written. Since τ is an involution with τ(ε_0) = ε_2, it should read τ(ε_2) = ε_0.

ideas.what: Using orientation-reversing involutions (reflections) acting on Dehn twists by inversion or permutation to transport relations: the extended mapping class group with real structures.
ideas.modern_name: Extended mapping class group Γ_{g,n}^± / real structures on moduli; action of complex conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Ivanov, Birman, etc.); for the Galois/Teichmüller setting, Grothendieck's school (Lochak, Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller tower and Galois action; the explicit treatment of reflections is unsure

ideas.what: Presentation of Γ_{1,1}: braid relation plus (ε_1ε_0)^6 = (ε_0ε_1ε_0)^4 = 1, and (ab)^3 = (aba)^2.
ideas.modern_name: SL_2(Z) presentation / mapping class group of punctured torus

deep.surprise_reason: Routine computational sheet: classical braid and SL_2(Z) relations and the action of reflections on twists, consistent with the published Lego-Teichmüller programme. There is no new result, and one relation is stated in a context where it needs care.
transcription_corrections: The second symbol list reads roughly 'ε, ε^*, ε̄'' (with a bar or emphasis), matching the curves labelled in the drawing.
Under ε_0ε_1ε_0 the label is σ_0, not ρ_0; ε_1ε_0 is labelled ρ_0^{-1}.
